tasks.short: Evaluate hearing or speech and language test results, barium swallow results, or medical or background information to diagnose and plan treatment for speech, language, fluency, voice, or swallowing disorders.

steps.what: Read the posted hearing, speech, barium swallow and background card.
Evaluate those results to diagnose speech, language, fluency, voice or swallowing disorders.
Plan treatment from the medical information with the patient.

tasks.design: The speech therapist reads a posted results card in {DOCS} with test name, date, score and examiner. They still evaluate the results, record the diagnosis, and plan treatment with the patient. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The diagnosis is a judgement across hearing, speech and swallowing results. A model that diagnosed would be decision software.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted card with test name, date, score and examiner can shorten only the read. The diagnosis and the plan stay with the speech therapist.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong diagnosis can harm the patient. That judgement does not become a rule.
tasks.human_edge: The speech therapist decides the diagnosis and the plan. A posted score decides neither.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the diagnosis and the plan talk. A little less time goes to hunting for a posted result.

reach.task: Post hearing scores on the results card before the speech therapist reads them.
reach.learn: A blank score is not a zero. When the card is missing, the speech therapist opens the source document and the read is not shorter.

evidence.claim: MDR is listed in AI Act Annex I. This task does not put diagnosis or the treatment plan on a model.
AI that needs a notified body is high-risk. This task does not use such a model to diagnose or to plan treatment.
A solely automated decision with legal or similar significant effect needs an Article 22 basis. The speech therapist makes the diagnosis.
Hearing results, speech and language results, and a diagnosis are health data.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the task starts when a results card is already in {DOCS} and ends when the speech therapist has recorded a diagnosis and talked through treatment with the patient. It does not order tests.

Results-card fields are test name, date, score and examiner. The audiologist or the lab posts hearing results and barium swallow results. The speech therapist posts their own speech and language test, and that posting time sits in the evaluation step, which stays at full time. A blank score is not zero. If the card is missing, the read is not shorter and they open the source document.
Nothing in this task sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
unknowns: Whether barium swallow results sit in the same record as the speech tests.
What share of results are scans rather than posted fields.
Whether any client is a minor.
Whether results cards are posted today.
research_questions: Who posts hearing results and barium swallow results today?
What share of those results already have test name, date, score and examiner filled?

already_counted.description: Reading a short posted card instead of searching the source, still inside the read.
Time still spent evaluating the results and recording the diagnosis.
Time still spent planning treatment with the patient.

incremental.description: When a results-card column is renamed, the speech therapist checks that test name, date, score and examiner still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when no results card is posted. The high end assumes about three in five evaluations have a complete card, so only that share of the read is shorter. Diagnosis and the plan talk stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write reports and maintain proper documentation of information, such as client Medicaid or billing records or caseload activities, including the initial evaluation, treatment, progress, and discharge of clients.

steps.what: Read the posted card of client caseload activities.
Draft proper documentation, including the initial evaluation.

loop.input: Client, date, disorder, activity and score already on the session card.
loop.output: Report sentences for the initial evaluation, treatment, progress and discharge.
loop.check: The speech therapist rejects any sentence whose clinical claim is not on the card.
loop.stop: One rejection and the speech therapist writes the report. The loop does not try again.
loop.why_not_simpler: The sentences are not a copy of the card fields.

steps.what: Write reports of treatment, progress and discharge from that draft.
Maintain records of clients by storing the accepted report.
Add billing information and leave Medicaid claims unsent.

tasks.design: The speech therapist reads the session card in {DOCS}. A draft writes the report sentences from that card only. The speech therapist accepts or rewrites those sentences. A write then stores the accepted report in {DOCS}. The speech therapist notes billing information by hand. Nothing sends a Medicaid claim, a bill, or an alert, and nothing fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report sentences make clinical claims. A store without the speech therapist's acceptance would file text they had not checked.
tasks.enabler_now: The session card is a small set of fields, so a bounded loop can propose sentences and stop after one rejection.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a note that writes clinical sentences is a medical device is unresolved. The speech therapist remains responsible for the text that is stored.
tasks.human_edge: Only the speech therapist can accept a sentence, rewrite the report, or refuse a claim the card does not hold.
tasks.altitude: Less of the day is composing sentences from fields already on the card. The speech therapist still accepts every report and still writes the billing note.

reach.task: Store only the report the speech therapist has accepted.
reach.learn: An unaccepted sentence is not filed. This task does not send a Medicaid claim.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation; the clinician validates; the note goes into the clinical record. The homepage claims 15-20 minutes saved per consult and gives no method. This firm's saving is not that claim, and this design does not record the room.
Tandem's scribe and coding products carry MDR class IIa. That class is a fact about those products, not a certification of this design.

Capio Ramsay Santé reported 1,295 clinicians and 236,153 Tandem notes. Self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes, and median editing stayed 93 seconds. Three of seven authors are from the vendor. A person still edits. That result is not this firm's saving.
The treatment dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: know whether it is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor.
A solely automated decision needs an Article 22 basis. The speech therapist accepts the report text before it is stored.
Works-council consent under the named article applies when a tool records staff performance. This design does not record the session.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the task starts from a session card already in {DOCS} and ends with an accepted report stored there and a billing note written by hand. It does not send a claim or a bill.

Session-card fields are client name, date, disorder, activity done and score. The speech therapist posts that card at the end of the session, and that posting time sits in the session itself, which stays at full time on the in-person tasks. A blank activity or a blank score means the draft does not run and must not invent a claim. If the card is missing, the draft and the file write do not run.
The draft runs on the card inside the firm's record environment and does not leave it. It is unknown whether a model host would sit outside the firm. The design forbids sending the text out.
Ambient recording is not used. About half the session cards may be free text. In that case the draft and the file write do not run and the speech therapist writes the report.
unknowns: Whether this firm bills US Medicaid. This task does not send a claim either way.
Whether a recording tool is already in the room. This design does not use one.
Whether a DPIA is already in place for a writing tool.
What share of session cards have client, date, disorder, activity and score filled.
research_questions: What share of session cards have all five fields filled, rather than free text?
Does a works council exist, and has it consented to any recording tool?

already_counted.description: Reading the posted session card, still inside the read.
Accepting or rewriting the report. This time also covers acceptance of the sentence draft and of the file write.
Writing the billing note and leaving Medicaid claims unsent.

incremental.description: When a session-card column is renamed, the speech therapist checks that client, date, disorder, activity and score still line up, and rejects a sentence the new column would misstate.

approvals.approved_version: report sentences limited to the session card
the accepted report for this client and date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the session card is never posted. The high end assumes about half the cards are free text, so the sentence step and the file write do not run and the speech therapist writes the whole report. The high end sits a little under half the central saving. It is not a figure from another health system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor patients' progress and adjust treatments accordingly.

steps.what: Read the posted progress card before this session.
Monitor patients' progress and adjust treatments accordingly.

tasks.design: The speech therapist reads a posted progress card in {DOCS} before the session. They still watch the patient and adjust the treatment in the room. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adjusting treatment depends on watching the patient in the room. A posted line cannot see that.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted progress card can shorten only the read before the session.
tasks.still_hard: The adjustment can harm the patient if it is wrong. It stays a judgement in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The speech therapist watches the patient and changes the treatment. No notice does that.
tasks.altitude: The session is unchanged. A little less time goes to finding the last score.

reach.task: Hear treatment changes from the speech therapist, not from a notice.
reach.learn: A speech-progress card is not the occupational therapist's own plan.

evidence.claim: A solely automated decision with legal or similar significant effect needs an Article 22 basis. Adjusting treatment stays with the speech therapist.
AI that needs a notified body is high-risk. This task does not use a model to change treatment.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the task starts from a progress card already in {DOCS} and ends in the room when the speech therapist has adjusted the treatment. It does not notify another role.

Progress-card fields are client, goal, last score and last activity. The speech therapist posted them in a prior session note, and that posting time sits in the in-person session, which stays at full time. A blank score stays blank. If the card is missing, the read is not shorter.
Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no dashboard.
unknowns: Whether progress cards are posted today.
Whether any client is a minor.
research_questions: Who posts the progress card today, and how often is the last score blank?

already_counted.description: Reading the posted progress card before the session.
Watching the patient and adjusting treatment in the room.

incremental.description: When a progress-card column is renamed, the speech therapist checks that client, goal, last score and last activity still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when no progress card is posted. The high end assumes about three in five sessions have a complete card, so only that share of the read is shorter. Watching the patient and adjusting treatment stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop or implement treatment plans for problems such as stuttering, delayed language, swallowing disorders, or inappropriate pitch or harsh voice problems, based on own assessments and recommendations of physicians, psychologists, or social workers.

steps.what: Read recommendations of physicians, psychologists or social workers.
Develop treatment plans for stuttering, delayed language or swallowing disorders.
Implement plans for inappropriate pitch or harsh voice problems, based on assessments.

tasks.design: The speech therapist reads a posted recommendation card in {DOCS}. They still write the treatment plans and still carry them out with the patient. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan is a clinical judgement from the speech therapist's own assessment and from other people's recommendations.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted recommendation card can shorten only the read. The plan and the session stay manual.
tasks.still_hard: Carrying out a swallowing or voice plan with the patient cannot be handed to a model.
tasks.human_edge: The speech therapist writes the plan and carries it out. A recommendation card does not become the plan.
tasks.altitude: The week is still developing and carrying out plans. A little less time goes to finding a recommendation.

reach.task: Keep their recommendation on the card the speech therapist reads.
reach.learn: A blank recommendation is not a recommendation. The speech therapist does not invent one.

evidence.claim: MDR is listed in AI Act Annex I. This task does not use a model to write or carry out the treatment plan.
AI that needs a notified body is high-risk. Decision software is usually in that class. This task leaves the plan with the speech therapist.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the task starts from a recommendation card already in {DOCS} and ends when the speech therapist has written the plans and carried them out with the patient.

Recommendation-card fields are source role, date, problem and recommendation text. The physician, the psychologist or the social worker posted that note. Their writing time is theirs. A blank recommendation is not a recommendation, and the read is not shorter.
Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. A model does not write the plan.
unknowns: Whether recommendation notes from physicians, psychologists and social workers sit in the same record.
Whether any client is a minor.
research_questions: Which physician, psychologist and social worker notes are already in {DOCS} as source role, date, problem and recommendation text?

already_counted.description: Time still spent developing the treatment plans.
Time still spent carrying out the plans with the patient.

incremental.description: When a recommendation-card column is renamed, the speech therapist checks that source role, date, problem and recommendation text still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when no recommendation card is posted. The high end assumes about three in five plans have a complete card, so only that share of the read is shorter. Writing the plan and carrying it out stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the session: diagnosing, adjusting treatment, and carrying out the plan. Less of it is searching for a posted result or composing report sentences from fields already on the card.
reach: Result cards are posted by the audiologist, the physician, or the speech therapist before the step that reads them.
A model does not diagnose, choose a treatment, or write the plan.
The speech therapist still accepts every report before it is stored, and still tells the patient what changes.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report sentence the session card does not support
Refuse a model that diagnoses a speech, voice or swallowing disorder
Refuse a notice that changes the treatment during a session
role.ambitious_version: The cards are already posted. The speech therapist still diagnoses, adjusts the session, writes the plan, and accepts the report.
